evidence.testTitle: [MEDIA-009 MEDIA-012 DB-025] failed provider cleanup leaves inaccessible pending bytes across recreation until internal retry
evidence.scenarioScope: Exact pending-owner quota accounting during failure/recreation and known-ID cleanup; no claim about file-size enforcement or all quota cases.
evidence.rationale: Real independent accounts, production Worker SQLite and R2 paths, deterministic I/O faults and complete workerd recreation.
assertionDetails: Real R2 put writes bytes then raises, actual production rollback attempts provider delete and an injected provider failure produces safe 503 with no pending ID disclosed.
Exact pending row, owner quota SUM and actual object bytes survive runtime recreation; public owner/foreign reads remain 404 and unrelated ready file stays readable.

No Accounts DO alarm is scheduled in this fixture; after provider fault resets on recreation, a direct internal retry with the original owner and inspected opaque ID removes the row, quota and object.
Live IRC/event barriers demonstrate connected observers; absence of an undocumented deadline is not asserted as a timing-policy violation.

evidence.testTitle: [MEDIA-009 MEDIA-012 DB-025] stopping workerd during a completed R2 put preserves inaccessible pending reservation until known-id deletion
evidence.scenarioScope: Exact pending-owner quota accounting during failure/recreation and known-ID cleanup; no claim about file-size enforcement or all quota cases.
evidence.rationale: Real independent accounts, production Worker SQLite and R2 paths, deterministic I/O faults and complete workerd recreation.
assertionDetails: Actual R2 put finishes, then a test gate holds the production route before finalization; disposing workerd prevents a 201 and recreates the same persisted SQLite and bucket state twice.
Exact pending row, bytes and owner quota remain across recreations; public reads remain 404 for owner and foreign user while unrelated ready object and a healthy upload survive.
The owner can delete the reservation only after the test obtains its opaque ID from internal state; another user receives 404, and no client-facing listing endpoint was found.
Live IRC/event barriers surround the held operation and after recreation; no claim is made about offline event delivery or an unspecified cleanup deadline.

reviewDecision.decision: Retain unpublished R2 object metadata and its quota reservation until cleanup succeeds; automatic abandoned-pending recovery is not implemented.
reviewDecision.basis: A timer alone cannot establish that an outstanding provider write has completed; a late put can recreate an object after cleanup. Pending content remains inaccessible in these tests, while automatic recovery and quota release remain absent.
reviewDecision.notAcceptance: No published cleanup deadline was found or imposed, and the observation tests do not establish complete DB-016, file-size enforcement or denied-client-write coverage.
reviewDecision.nextReview: Before implementing leases, fencing, alarms or tombstones, define bounded retention and admission policies so permanent rechecks cannot generate unbounded metadata or provider cost.
reviewDecision.capabilityLimitation: Automatic recovery of abandoned pending R2 objects and quota reservations is not implemented; this observation does not itself establish a storage-quota bypass.
